items.name: RunEndBuffer
items.summary: A buffer of monotonically increasing, positive integers used to store run-ends.

methods.name: claim
methods.summary: Claim memory used by this buffer in the provided memory pool.

methods.name: get_end_physical_index
methods.summary: Returns the physical index at which the logical array ends.

methods.name: get_physical_index
methods.summary: Performs a binary search to find the physical index for the given logical index.

methods.name: get_physical_indices
methods.signature: fn get_physical_indices<I>(&self, logical_indices: &[I]) -> Result<Vec<usize>, I> where I: ArrowNativeType
methods.summary: Returns the physical indices corresponding to the provided logical indices.

methods.name: get_start_physical_index
methods.summary: Returns the physical index at which the logical array starts.

methods.name: is_empty
methods.summary: Returns true if this buffer is logically empty.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the logical length of the run-ends stored by this buffer.

methods.name: max_value
methods.summary: Returns the maximum run-end encoded in the underlying buffer; that is, the last physical run of the buffer. This does not take into account any logical slicing that may have occurred.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(run_ends: ScalarBuffer<E>, logical_offset: usize, logical_length: usize) -> Self
methods.summary: Create a new [`RunEndBuffer`] from a [`ScalarBuffer`], `logical_offset` and `logical_length`.

methods.name: new_unchecked
methods.signature: unsafe fn new_unchecked(run_ends: ScalarBuffer<E>, logical_offset: usize, logical_length: usize) -> Self
methods.summary: Create a new [`RunEndBuffer`] from a [`ScalarBuffer`], `logical_offset` and `logical_length`.

methods.name: offset
methods.summary: Returns the logical offset into the run-ends stored by this buffer.

methods.name: slice
methods.signature: fn slice(&self, logical_offset: usize, logical_length: usize) -> Self
methods.summary: Slices this [`RunEndBuffer`] by the provided `logical_offset` and `logical_length`.

methods.name: sliced_values
methods.summary: Returns an iterator yielding run ends adjusted for the logical slice.

methods.name: values
methods.summary: Returns the physical (**unsliced**) run ends of this buffer.
